title: SciPy spsolve / SuperLU SUPERLU_MALLOC failure despite available RAM
text:
SciPy spsolve / SuperLU SUPERLU_MALLOC failure despite available RAM

I am trying to solve a large sparse linear system in Python3.12 using SciPy. The linux server has 48 threads and 192 GB RAM . My code uses scipy.sparse.linalg.spsolve() on a sparse matrix i solved N = 3000 on my laptop which has 16GB of ram, then i get server with 48GB of ram and solve N=3500 and it consumed about 30Gb of ram then solve N=4000 and it consumed about 40GB of ram then i get a server with 96GB of ram and solve N = 4500 , and i don't remember its ram consumption. after that i try to solve N=5000 which lead to SuperLU fails as following then i tried server with 192GB of ram and again SuperLU fails as follow: computing N = 5000 ... Traceback (most recent call last): File "/home/Xxlonely/Desktop/code/./chamekon.py", line 113, in <module> p = fixation_probability(N) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/home/Xxlonely/Desktop/code/./chamekon.py", line 97, in fixation_probability solution = spsolve(A, rhs) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/home/Xxlonely/Desktop/code/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/scipy/sparse/linalg/_dsolve/linsolve.py", line 289, in spsolve x, info = _superlu.gssv(N, A.nnz, A.data, indices, indptr, ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ RuntimeError: SUPERLU_MALLOC fails for buf in intCalloc() at line 173 in file ../scipy/sparse/linalg/_dsolve/SuperLU/SRC/memory.c At the time of the error, the system was only showing around 3% RAM usage , so there appeared to be plenty of free memory. The my original code is: import numpy as np from scipy.sparse import lil_matrix from scipy.sparse.linalg import spsolve def fixation_probability(N): M = N + 2 # All non-monochromatic states are transient. states = [] for r in range(M + 1): for b in range(M - r + 1): g = M - r - b # Exclude the three monochromatic states. if (r == M and b == 0 and g == 0): continue if (r == 0 and b == M and g == 0): continue if (r == 0 and b == 0 and g == M): continue states.append((r, b, g)) index = {state: i for i, state in enumerate(states)} nstates = len(states) A = lil_matrix((nstates, nstates), dtype=float) rhs = np.zeros(nstates) def boundary_value(state): """Return P_R on a state with exactly two colours.""" r, b, g = state # Monochromatic states if r == M and b == 0 and g == 0: return 1.0 if r == 0 and b == M and g == 0: return 0.0 if r == 0 and b == 0 and g == M: return 0.0 # Red-green boundary: b = 0 if b == 0: return 0 # Red-blue boundary: g = 0 if g == 0: return 1 # Blue-green boundary: r = 0 if r == 0: return 0.0 return None for state, i in index.items(): r, b, g = state w1 = r * b w2 = b * g w3 = g * r total = w1 + w2 + w3 # Diagonal coefficient. A[i, i] = total transitions = [ (w1, (r + 1, b - 1, g)), (w2, (r, b + 1, g - 1)), (w3, (r - 1, b, g + 1)), ] for weight, new_state in transitions: if weight == 0: continue value = boundary_value(new_state) if value is not None: # Absorbing or two-colour boundary state. rhs[i] += weight * value else: # Interior transient state. j = index[new_state] A[i, j] -= weight # Convert to CSR for the sparse solver. A = A.tocsr() solution = spsolve(A, rhs) return solution[index[(1, 1, N)]] # ------------------------------------------------------------ # Compute the table # ------------------------------------------------------------ Ns = [5000] print(f"{'N':>6} {'P_R(1,1,N)':>20} {'N*P_R(1,1,N)':>20}") print("-" * 50) for N in Ns: print(f"computing N = {N} ...") p = fixation_probability(N) print(f"{N:6d} {p:20.12f} {N*p:20.12f}") print() print("Conjectured limit:") C = 2 * np.pi / (3 * np.sqrt(3)) print(f"C = {C:.12f}") How could I solve a larger instance (e.g., N = 5000 )? Since SciPy is essentially a wrapper around lower-level libraries, what would be the best way to address this problem?

title: FastAPI Form() with List[Type] sends array as comma-separated string ("2,5") causing 422 parsing error in Swagger UI
text:
FastAPI Form() with List[Type] sends array as comma-separated string ("2,5") causing 422 parsing error in Swagger UI

Here's a Minimal, Reproducible Example: from fastapi import FastAPI, Form from typing import Annotated, List app = FastAPI() @app.post('/') def create(arr: Annotated[List[int], Form()] = []): return arr Sending a request with 2 or more elements in arr yields this response: { "detail": [ { "type": "int_parsing", "loc": [ "body", "arr", 0 ], "msg": "Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer", "input": "1,5" } ] } but sending a request where arr contains no elements or exactly 1 element yields the expected response where the array itself is returned. I tried changing the Form() to Form(...) but nothing changes. interestingly enough changing List[int] to List[str] and sending an array with multiple strings doesn't return a 422 but rather returns an array with exactly one string element containing the comma separated elements: [ "First String,2nd String,Number 3" ] Somebody else experienced this issue HERE .

Python 3.14.6 IDE: VS Code Version 1.134.0 (Pylance) class EventHandler: def post_event(self, event: str): print(event) def create_value_property[V](name: str) -> property: def get(self) -> V: return getattr(self, f"_{name}") def set(self, value: V) -> None: prev_value = getattr(self, f"_{name}") if value == prev_value: return setattr(self, f"_{name}", value) self.event_handler.post_event(f"{name} value changed: {value}") return property(get, set) class Custom[V]: def __init__(self, val1: V, val2: V, val3: V) -> None: self._val1: V = val1 self._val2: V = val2 self._val3: V = val3 self.event_handler: EventHandler = EventHandler() val1: property = create_value_property('val1') val2: property = create_value_property('val2') val3: property = create_value_property('val3') custom = Custom[int](1,1,1) a = custom.val1 # a and custom.val1 report type Any custom.val1 = 2 custom.val2 = 3 custom.val3 = 4 I was able to figure out a middle ground. I was trying to avoid defining the same @setter for each property by using create_value_property . Instead I can do something like this and the typing works. I'm still curious if I can get the initial method working as it is much cleaner. def set_value[V](self, attr: V, value: V) -> None: if attr == value: return prev_val = attr attr = value self.event_handler.post_event(f"{attr} value changed: {value}") class Rev2[V]: def __init__(self, val1: V) -> None: self._val1: V = val1 self.event_handler: EventHandler = EventHandler() @property def val1(self) -> V: return self._val1 @val1.setter def val1(self, value: V) -> None: set_value(self, self._val1, value) An attempt with descriptors as suggested in the comments (with some functionality stripped out). Now the type inferred by the type checker for val1 is Unknown . class Prop[V]: def __set_name__(self, owner, name) -> None: self.name = name def __get__(self, instance, owner) -> V: return instance.__dict__.get(self.name) def __set__(self, instance, value) -> None: instance.__dict__[self.name] = value print(f"value set") class Rev3[V]: Val1 = Prop() rev3 = Rev3() rev3.Val1

title: Run an async function weekly at a specific time
text:
Run an async function weekly at a specific time

I am looking for a way to run a task starting at a certain time and then repeating every X amount of time afterwards for my bot. For example, run a function at Sunday 7:00pm and then every week afterwards. As it stands I have the current code and am getting the following error shown below. It would be preferable to use the same libraries and have it be async so it isn't blocking other bot functions. import asyncio from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta import pytz days = { "Monday": 0, "Tuesday": 1, "Wednesday": 2, "Thursday": 3, "Friday": 4, "Saturday": 5, "Sunday": 6, } def delay_until(day: str, hour: int): if ( day.capitalize() not in days or day.capitalize() != "Tomorrow" or hour < 0 or hour > 24 ): return "Invalid date provided" # Get the next day coming up, i.e. the next Monday today = datetime.now(tz=pytz.utc).date() if day.capitalize() == "Tomorrow": target_day = today + timedelta(days=1) else: target_day = today + timedelta( days=(days[day.capitalize()] - today.weekday()) % 7 ) # Add the hours onto the date to make the datetime full_datetime: datetime = datetime( year=target_day.year, month=target_day.month, day=target_day.day, hour=hour, tzinfo=pytz.utc, ) # Get the time from the target datetime to now in seconds delta = full_datetime - datetime.now(tz=pytz.utc) delay: float = delta.total_seconds() return delay # Function to schedule a task to run after a given delay and time to loop async def schedule(delay: float, loop_time: float, function, *args, **kwargs): await asyncio.sleep(delay) while True: await asyncio.gather(function(*args, **kwargs), asyncio.sleep(loop_time)) def time_from_string(time: int, unit: str): match unit: case "week": return time * 604800 case "day": return time * 86400 def demo_fx(): print("hello world") async def sample_task(): await schedule( delay=delay_until("Sunday", 21), loop_time=time_from_string(1, "week"), function=demo_fx(), ) print(asyncio.run(sample_task())) Output: hello world Traceback (most recent call last): File "/home/bptsoum/Programming/Tinkering/scrap.py", line 153, in <module> print(asyncio.run(sample_task())) ~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/usr/lib/python3.14/asyncio/runners.py", line 205, in run return runner.run(main) ~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^ File "/usr/lib/python3.14/asyncio/runners.py", line 128, in run return self._loop.run_until_complete(task) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^ File "/usr/lib/python3.14/asyncio/base_events.py", line 720, in run_until_complete return future.result() ~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^ File "/home/bptsoum/Programming/Tinkering/scrap.py", line 147, in sample_task await schedule( ...<3 lines>... ) File "/home/bptsoum/Programming/Tinkering/scrap.py", line 131, in schedule await asyncio.sleep(delay) File "/usr/lib/python3.14/asyncio/tasks.py", line 692, in sleep if delay <= 0: ^^^^^^^^^^ TypeError: '<=' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'int'
